title: An animation studio that renders at night
summary: A Guadalajara studio renders a short film overnight on 200 VMs that read the same scenes. The artists work from their office and no scene can be lost.

requirements.1: {{s1}} holds the project folder that hundreds of Linux servers mount at the same time over NFS, available in both fault domains.
requirements.2: {{s2}} keeps last night's version of the project folder, so a scene someone deletes by mistake can be recovered.
requirements.3: {{s3}} stores the finished frames for years; they are read over HTTP from the internet and do not depend on any instance.
requirements.4: {{s4}} provides the render nodes: they can shut down with seconds or minutes of notice because the job resumes, and the lowest price with no commitment matters.
requirements.5: {{s5}} joins the office to the cloud network today, encrypted, over the internet it already has.
requirements.6: The artists work at the studio office in Guadalajara and upload their scenes from there.

s1.explanation: OCI File Storage uses NFSv3; each mount target lives in a subnet and accepts up to 100,000 NFS connections. Within the availability domain it replicates synchronously and has failover.
s1.hint_cue: mount at the same time over NFS

s2.explanation: A File Storage snapshot is a consistent point-in-time view kept under .snapshot/name at the root of the file system, where the deleted scene can be copied back from.

s3.explanation: Object Storage is a regional service that does not depend on any compute instance; it is read from the internet or from within the cloud and stores data redundantly across several servers.
s3.hint_cue: do not depend on any instance

s4.explanation: Preemptible instances can be terminated at any time, with an event two minutes before, and cost 50% less than on-demand capacity: they suit work that tolerates interruptions.

s5.explanation: Site-to-Site VPN uses public internet lines and encrypts with IPsec all communication between the office and the VCN, which goes through the DRG.
s5.hint_cue: over the internet it already has

oci-block-volume.s1: A block volume is used as an instance's hard drive; attaching it to several at once requires installing a cluster-aware solution, and it is not an NFS folder.
oci-block-volume.s3: A block volume is used as an instance's hard drive; it does not store objects that are read over HTTP from the internet.

oci-fss-replication.s2: Replication gives the target the same file and folder structure as the source and, at each interval, deletes the previous replication snapshot: it does not keep last night's version.
oci-fss-replication.s1: Replication copies a file system that already exists; on its own it is not the folder the servers mount.

oci-capacity-reservation.s4: A capacity reservation sets instances aside, but they are billed at the standard rate and unused capacity is billed at 85%: it does not make the nodes cheaper.

oci-fastconnect.s5: FastConnect creates a dedicated, private connection between the data center and Oracle Cloud, not the encrypted tunnel over the internet the office already has.
